newsitem.title: KENYA: U.S., Japan criticise Kenya for beatings.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan criticise Kenya for beatings.

text.p: The United States and Japan criticised Kenya on Tuesday for how police had roughed up opposition legislators after a church service and called on the government to bring those involved to justice.

Witnesses said opposition members of parliament Paul Muite and Kiraitu Murungi, along with a number of their supporters, were attacked after leaving a Sunday church service during a visit to Nyeri in central Kenya.

"Officially sanctioned violence during this election year inhibits Kenyan citizens from exercising their constitutionally guaranteed freedoms and mars the image of Kenya as a democratic country," a statement from the U.S. embassy said.
The statement from the American embassy said the Japanese embassy agreed with the protest.
President Daniel arap Moi, aged 72 and in power since 1978, must call elections within the next year.

The opposition has accused the government of abusing its position to ensure victory in the polls by harassing opponents, denying them access to broadcast media and introducing controversial new identity cards.
But the opposition suffers deep internal divisions and is currently unable to form a united front to defeat the ruling Kenya African National Union party.
